sections.h2: Where is the Washington County recorder's office?
sections.html:
The Washington County recorder works from the courthouse at 205 Putnam Street, Marietta, OH 45750. Call 740-373-6623, extension 2223 or 2225, or fax 740-373-9643. Counter hours are 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, Monday to Friday, with legal holidays excluded.

Every document that conveys or burdens land in the county goes into the recorder's permanent archive, and the filing fees go to the county's general fund. A deed for any Washington County parcel, whether the owner lives in Marietta or in Belpre, Beverly or Waterford, ends up at this counter or in its e-recording queue.

sections.h2: What is Washington County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Washington County is the oldest county in Ohio, proclaimed on July 27, 1788 with settlement at Marietta beginning on April 7 of that year. Its 640 square miles rank fifth among Ohio counties by land area, and the Ohio River forms the southern and eastern line. The Muskingum River, the Little Muskingum, Duck Creek and the Little Hocking River all run to the Ohio from inside the county.

Marietta serves as seat and largest city. Marietta College, Washington State College of Ohio and the county career center are all there. The present courthouse dates from 1901. Settlement began when a New England group, the Ohio Company, bought land on the Ohio and Muskingum Rivers, and Fort Harmar at the confluence shaped that choice. Early outposts included Belpre downriver and Beverly up the Muskingum, so the county's oldest deeds trace back to the 1780s and 1790s.

Census 2020 shows 27,987 homes and apartments in the county, about three of every four occupied homes lived in by their owners, and a majority of residents outside urban areas. River-valley houses in older neighborhoods and rural parcels outside town call for different paperwork, which is why the courthouse offices below matter.

sections.h2: Which Washington County office does what in a sale?
sections.html:
The auditor and recorder share the courthouse at 205 Putnam Street and the 740-373-6623 main line, which lets a seller finish two stops in one visit. The extensions below come from the auditor's website and the recorder's page.

Washington County courthouse extensions for deed-related tasks (county auditor and recorder pages)
TaskOfficeExtension
Real estate transfersAuditor2124
Property appraisal valueAuditor2141
Report new construction or demolitionAuditor2141
Homestead exemptionsAuditor2123
Tax mapAuditor2161
Recording a deed or mortgageRecorder2223 or 2225

The auditor's site also posts sales reports, and the auditor's counter keeps the same weekday hours as the recorder, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm.

sections.h2: How does the Washington County recorder take documents?
sections.html:
Paper goes to the counter, and electronic filing runs through approved vendors. The recorder's page names Corporation Service Company at 866-652-0111 and eRecording Partners Network at 888-325-3365. Simplifile is also listed, with a note that it cannot be used for deeds.

The county's FAQ gives a document turnaround of three days. It also spells out how payment errors are handled: filings that arrive under the correct fee are returned, and filings over by $5.00 or more are usually returned too, while an overage under $5.00 is sent back in cash. Mailing the exact amount avoids the delay.

For searching, the recorder's page links to an online records search and a second cloud-based search. The FAQ also lists uslandrecords.com as a no-charge search link.

sections.h2: What fees does Ohio set for recording in Washington County?
sections.html:
Ohio's section 317.32 builds each charge from two equal halves. The opening two pages cost $17 and $17, later pages cost $4 and $4 apiece, and a preservation surcharge is allowed up to $5. Ask the recorder which surcharge figure Washington County applies, since the statute sets only the cap.

  • A certified copy is $1 plus $1 a page, with the seal at 50 cents plus 50 cents.
  • Plats and maps are charged by the square inch, with a $20 plus $20 minimum.
  • Declarations under the living will and health care power of attorney statutes run $17 to $20 plus the same range again.
  • County land reutilization corporations are exempt from recorder fees.

sections.h2: What does the Washington County auditor charge on a transfer?
sections.html:
The auditor's FAQ states the Washington County conveyance fee as $.40 per $100 of value. That rate fits the statute's two layers, ten cents per hundred under section 319.54 and up to thirty cents more where commissioners adopted a tax under section 322.02. The auditor's website also has a conveyance calculator, and extension 2124 handles real estate transfers.

Transfers that fall into an exempt class pay nothing, though the paperwork still names the class. The cases that arise most in family sales:

  • A gift from one spouse to the other, or from a parent to a child.
  • A deed that corrects an earlier one.
  • A transfer made only as security for a loan.
  • A distribution among heirs where no money is paid.
  • A deed placing the house in a trust the owner can revoke.

The auditor's homestead page lists DTE Form 101, a Statement of Conveyance of Homestead Property, for sales of a home that carries the homestead reduction.

sections.h2: How does Washington County value and bill a home for tax?
sections.html:
By the auditor's account, every parcel is revalued at market once in six years, and the Ohio Tax Commissioner typically orders a statistical adjustment three years later using actual county sales. Property appraisal questions go to extension 2141, and the website has a tax estimator and a delinquency report.

Disputes over value go to the county Board of Revision, which the auditor's FAQ describes as a county commissioner, the treasurer and the auditor sitting together. The complaint form is due by March 31, and the hearings usually fall in April and May. Bring an appraisal report or current sales of similar houses in your neighborhood.

The auditor's pages describe the relief programs that follow a house from seller to buyer in practice:

  • Homestead for seniors 65 and over and permanently and totally disabled owners, using form DTE 105A. The exemptions page says it shields $25,000 of market value, and disabled veterans can shield $50,000.
  • The owner occupancy reduction of 2 1/2 percent for the home you own and live in, applied for between January 1 and December 31 at no cost.
  • CAUV farm value for at least 10 acres of crops, animals or commercial timber, with a one-time $25 filing fee and a yearly renewal. Missing a renewal costs the savings and brings a payback of the previous three years.

The treasurer, at the same courthouse, collects real estate and manufactured home tax. Call 740-373-6623 and choose option 3 and then 2, any weekday from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm. Manufactured and mobile homes must be registered with the auditor within 30 days of placement in the county, and moving one takes a $5 permit.

faqs.q: What is the Washington County recorder's phone number?
faqs.a: Call 740-373-6623 and ask for extension 2223 or 2225. Visit the courthouse at 205 Putnam Street in Marietta between 8:00 am and 4:30 pm on weekdays.

faqs.q: Can a deed be e-recorded in Washington County?
faqs.a: Yes, through Corporation Service Company or eRecording Partners Network. The recorder's page adds that Simplifile cannot be used to record deeds.

faqs.q: How long does recording take in Washington County?
faqs.a: The county FAQ gives three days. Having the auditor's endorsement and the exact fee on the deed keeps the filing from being returned.

faqs.q: What happens if I send the wrong fee to the Washington County recorder?
faqs.a: A short payment is returned. A payment over by $5.00 or more is usually returned as well, and an overage under $5.00 comes back in cash, according to the recorder's FAQ.

faqs.q: Which Washington County office handles a real estate transfer before recording?
faqs.a: The auditor, at extension 2124 off 740-373-6623. The auditor takes the statement of value and the conveyance fee, endorses the deed, and passes it along to the recorder.
